To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

frictionless rigid pentagonal particles, in contrast to frictionless rigid circular particles, exhibit internal friction and that, as a consequence of the internal friction, the shear flow of frictionless rigid polygonal particles is anisotropic.
the friction coefficient of frictionless pentagons is 0.183 ± 0.008 and that the solid fraction of pentagons under shear coincides with the isotropic random close packing fraction.

(i) the internal friction coefficient is the same for frictionless disks and pentagons and (ii) the solid fraction is the same under isotropic and sheared configurations for both disk and pentagon packings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanical behavior of frictionless granular materials, which is of interest for many applications.
the rheology of frictionless granular media, and we show that internal friction can be achieved even without frictional contacts between particles.
the mechanical properties of frictionless packings of rigid pentagons under shear, and the results obtained are compared to the properties of packings of disks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the internal friction is a direct consequence of the anisotropic structure induced by shear, while dilatancy results from a balance between the tendency of particles to collapse and to rearrange.
the internal friction coefficient and dilatancy of a granular material are two independent properties that do not necessarily correlate.
the internal friction of frictionless pentagons in shear is not related to the macroscopic dilancy of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the absence of friction, the shear flow of pentagonal grains is characterized by an internal friction but no macroscopic dilation, while in the presence of friction the system dilates under shear but the internal friction coefficient is not affected by the presence of friction.
the absence of friction is a necessary condition for the absence of dilatance, and that the presence of anisotropy is a necessary condition of internal friction.
, at least for the case of pentagons, internal friction and dilatancy are two separate phenomena that do not go hand in hand.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, contrary to common belief, the absence of macroscopic dilatant response is not a signature of frictionless particles.
the absence of macroscopic dilatation is not a unique feature of frictionless particles, and that it can be observed in assemblies of frictionless polygons.
the internal friction coefficient of a granular material can be measured independently of the presence or absence of dilatant flow.
